title: Flag the bad export lines
prompt: HR wants to fix broken lines at the source, so nothing may be dropped. Write `solve(employees_raw)` so it reads the saved export, keeps every employee line, and adds `bad_line`: the raw text of each line that didn't fit, and NULL for good lines.
rules: Fields are separated by `;`, the first line is a header (not an employee), and quoted values can contain `;`.
Columns: `employee_id STRING, full_name STRING, job_title STRING, department STRING, salary DECIMAL(10,2), hire_date DATE`, then `bad_line STRING`.
Keep every employee line. Values that couldn't be read are NULL, and `bad_line` holds the line exactly as it arrived.
Return all seven columns, in this order.
hints: Start from the same read as a clean import: separator, header and schema.
Add `bad_line STRING` to the end of the schema string.
The default mode keeps bad lines; `columnNameOfCorruptRecord="bad_line"` tells Spark where to put their raw text.
starter:
def solve(employees_raw):
    path = "/tmp/hr/employees"
    employees_raw.write.mode("overwrite").text(path)
    # Read the file at `path` as CSV and return every line with bad_line.
    return employees_raw
